durable_order_check.independently_proves: The exact harness and precommit were durable in repository history before the result artifact was persisted.
durable_order_check.does_not_independently_prove: The first OS-process execution began only after precommit readback; no independently timestamped execution-start event or external run log was found in the audited artifact set. The checkpoint self-reports that order.

observed_case_family: prewire SIGKILL after durable local INTENT
controller SIGKILL after provider durable commit and before HTTP response is released/read
provider os._exit after durable effect commit and before HTTP response send
code_and_result_recalculation.durability_mechanism: separate controller/provider SQLite databases with WAL and synchronous=FULL; separate provider/controller OS processes; loopback HTTP

public_primary_sources.verified: The draft describes Idempotency-Key as a way to make non-idempotent HTTP methods fault-tolerant.
public_primary_sources.scope_correction: Datatracker marks revision -07 expired and archived, last updated 2025-10-15 and expired 2026-04-18. It is not a current RFC/active standards guarantee.

public_primary_sources.source: Stripe API v2 overview and Advanced error handling
public_primary_sources.verified: Stripe documents caller-supplied Idempotency-Key semantics and recommends same-key/same-parameter retries after network errors when the client cannot know whether Stripe received the request.
public_primary_sources.scope_correction: API v2 does not simply promise the exact previously stored response for every retry: successful operations skip new changes and return an updated response, failed/partial operations can be re-executed without new side effects, and replay identity is scoped to same API/account or sandbox within 30 days. API v1 has different 24-hour/cached-response semantics.

material_scope_corrections.finding: The authored reconcilable provider is not a pure reconcile-only provider.
material_scope_corrections.evidence: Its POST /execute path first queries effect by eval_id and reuses the prior score instead of inserting a second effect when one exists. The test therefore bundles query-by-ID reconciliation with a sequential idempotent-like execute behavior.
material_scope_corrections.consequence: The six cases support the tested reconcilable bundle and neither mode; they do not independently establish a reconcile-only provider class.

material_scope_corrections.finding: The local provider does not database-enforce effect uniqueness by eval_id and the harness does not test concurrent duplicate POSTs.
material_scope_corrections.evidence: The effect table has no UNIQUE constraint on eval_id. Sequential POST code performs SELECT-then-INSERT, but no two controllers/concurrent same-eval_id requests are exercised.
material_scope_corrections.consequence: Do not promote 'provider operation identity' to a concurrent sink-side exactly-once/fencing guarantee.

material_scope_corrections.finding: Git history independently proves durable harness/precommit precede result persistence, but not the exact instant of first execution.
material_scope_corrections.evidence: Harness commit db9066 is an ancestor of precommit 86dbcb; precommit is an ancestor of result 098dfc. The result artifact has no independent execution-start timestamp/log.

material_scope_corrections.finding: The cited IETF Idempotency-Key document is expired/archived as of the audited date and should be treated as design precedent, not an active standard.

supported_conclusions_after_correction: The current self_improvement HTTP leaf is exactly bound to the current root22/config7 assignment at its durable checkpoint commit and remains so at the verifier frozen snapshot.

The exact authored six-case loopback harness records one provider effect and no replayed execute in the two post-provider-commit reconcilable crash cases; neither mode fails closed to UNKNOWN/BLOCKED_UNKNOWN without a second execute.
A terminal second controller resume is coded to return before provider access and the result records zero additional execute/reconcile calls for all six cases.
The worker's narrow scope statement—loopback HTTP, separate local processes/stores, no arbitrary remote-provider guarantee—is source-correct and should be preserved.
not_directly_tested: concurrent duplicate execute requests from multiple controllers
sink-side UNIQUE/CAS/fencing enforcement by semantic operation identity
independently observed precommit-readback timestamp before first executable process start
exact_next_verification: Do not repeat this six-case loopback harness unless a new concrete race is added.

Verify the next source-bound provider contract mapping only if it distinguishes idempotent+reconcile, idempotent-only, reconcile-only and neither with exact API-version/key-scope/payload-mismatch/retention/recovery semantics.
Require an explicit concurrent same-operation negative/positive control or sink-side unique/CAS/fence before treating provider operation identity as a concurrency-safe exactly-once property.

For any future durable-precommit acceptance claim, prefer an independently inspectable execution-start trace or run identity that is causally after the precommit readback, not only precommit-before-result Git ancestry.
